**Switching from Main Campus to Online BA in Criminology**

To transition from main campus at Texas Tech University to the fully online Bachelor of Arts in Criminology, here’s what you need to do:

---

**1. Review Program Format and Requirements**
- The Online BA in Criminology is 100% asynchronous, allowing you to complete coursework from anywhere.
- You can view degree and course details here: [Criminology, B.A. – Online](https://catalog.ttu.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=26&poid=17224&hl=Criminology%2C+B.A.+-+Online&returnto=search)

---

**2. Steps to Switch to Online**

- **Submit a Transition Request:**  
  Go to Raiderlink, then Student Dashboard under the Registrar tab, and fill out the “Transition to 100% Online” form. This is a formal application and can be denied, so ensure you meet all requirements.

- **Meet with Your Academic Advisor:**  
  Discuss your intention to switch to online, how your 56 credits will apply to the online BA in Criminology, and how to declare a minor in Forensic Science. Your advisor will help you map out your remaining courses and ensure you’re on track for graduation.

- **Update Your Degree Plan:**  
  Your advisor will help you update your degree plan to reflect the online BA in Criminology and the Forensic Science minor. They will also review which of your completed credits will transfer directly into the online program.

- **Register for Online Courses:**  
  Once your transition is approved, you’ll register for online courses through Raiderlink. Your Online Student Advocate can assist with course planning and registration.

---

**3. Additional Considerations**

- **Residency Requirements:**  
  There may be a minimum number of credits you must complete through Texas Tech Online to graduate. Your advisor can clarify this based on your situation.

- **Financial Aid and Billing:**  
  Switching to online may affect your tuition, fees, and financial aid. Contact Student Business Services (sbs@ttu.edu, 806.742.3272) for billing questions.

- **Support Services:**  
  As an online student, you’ll have access to Online Student Advocates, tutoring, and other support resources.

---

**4. Declaring a Minor in Forensic Science**

- Work with your advisor to declare the Forensic Science minor and ensure you meet all requirements for both your major and minor.
- Confirm that all minor courses are available online or discuss alternatives if some are only offered on campus.

---

**5. Next Steps**

- Log in to Raiderlink and submit the “Transition to 100% Online” form.
- Schedule a meeting with your academic advisor to review your degree plan and discuss your transition.
- Contact your Online Student Advocate for additional support with registration and planning.

---
